text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.
- Justice Minister Gerd Liv Valla has ruled that Bosnian refugees who return to their home country will be granted a residence permit in Norway if they decide to leave Bosnia again within two years.
- The use of force in the treatment of the mentally handicapped is against international human rights standards, according to the Norwegian lawyers association.

- More and more passengers at Norwegian airports are trying to travel with illegal objects such as harpoons, axes, crowbars and knives. The number of illegal objects confiscated in 1996 rose 12.5 percent from the year before.
- Environment Minister Torbjoern Berntsen faces stiff criticism after postponing the construction of a paper recycling plant.

- Postbanken's acquisition of a massive block of shares in insurer Storebrand on Friday means that state-owned companies will hold 33 percent of the future Christiania Group if the merger with Christiania Bank goes through.
- Since Christmas oil prices have fallen by as much as 30 percent. It is not impossible that prices could fall to $14 per barrel, says oil analyst Christopher Stoeren at Norwegian Oil Trading.
- Norway's largest commercial bank Den Norske Bank has increased it stake in Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbanken) to 15.2 percent.
